title: Derived Hom computed by a bounded-above projective resolution
statement: Let $A$ be a ring, let $F$ and $G$ be $A$-modules [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], and let $E^\bullet\to F[0]$ be a quasi-isomorphism from a bounded-above complex of projective $A$-modules. Then the cochain complex $\operatorname{Hom}_A^\bullet(E^\bullet,G[0])$ represents $R\operatorname{Hom}_A(F[0],G[0])$, and hence its $i$-th cohomology is canonically $H^i(R\operatorname{Hom}_A(F[0],G[0]))$ for every $i\in\mathbf Z$ [def-pur-derived-internal-hom].

source.place: derived Hom computed from projective resolutions (the projective-resolution construction of RHom); compare More on Algebra Tag 0A64 and Derived Categories Tag 06XR

proof.text: Restriction to the slice at an object of the one-point discrete site preserves projective objects: the restriction/pushforward adjunction is an equivalence, since its unit and counit are sectionwise images of isomorphisms. Restrict E termwise and transfer its upper support bound and projective terms; apply CochainComplex.isKProjective_of_projective. Restriction sends a quasi-isomorphism s to a quasi-isomorphism by lem-pur-localized-module-restriction-quasi-iso. By lem-pur-hom-complex-sections-homotopy-naturality, the map on degree-n section homology of Hom(E,s) is postcomposition by the shifted restricted s in the homotopy category. The two bijections IsKProjective.Qh_map_bijective identify it with postcomposition by an isomorphism in the derived category; composing with its inverse proves bijectivity. Apply lem-pur-quasi-iso-of-sections to obtain the sheaf quasi-isomorphism Hom(E,s), for any quasi-isomorphism s.

For any functorial K-injective replacement (I,eta), apply Step 1 to eta at G[0]. Apply lem-pur-rhom-well-defined to the identity of I(G[0]) and e to show that Hom(F[0],I(G[0])) to Hom(E,I(G[0])) is a quasi-isomorphism. Q inverts these maps, proving both IsIso clauses for every replacement. Choose the canonical K-injective resolution, evaluate derivedInternalHom_comparison at (F[0],G[0]), and compose Q Hom(E,eta), the inverse of Q Hom(e,I(G[0])), and the inverse comparison. This gives the required representing isomorphism.

For every integer i apply DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor to the representing isomorphism and prepend the inverse of DerivedCategory.homologyFunctorFactors at Hom(E,G[0]). This gives the cohomology identification with exactly the statement's two objects, including negative degrees.
